beats.act: the game, both effects, their jobs
beats.narration_text: Walker Rudy is a 2D side-scroller in Godot four point seven, on the Compatibility renderer. Effect A, slash sparks, is a burst. Its job: show where and when the cut can land, because the sword's hitbox is live for only point one five seconds of a point three second swing, fifty pixels in front of him. Its event is that hitbox going live. Effect B, run dust, is a trail. Its job: show that he is running, which way, and where his feet meet the ground. Its condition: in control, on the floor, and moving.

shot.observation: Two frames of the film's own Movie Maker capture of the real Main at d0ed415: two SlashSparks bursts alive during fast cuts, and RunDust's trail behind Rudy while he runs.

beats.act: the three parts of a particle system
beats.narration_text: Every particle system has three parts. Emission: how many, how often, how long. Line one oh eight: twenty-eight sparks, all at once. Process: how each particle moves and changes over its life. Line seventy-nine sets gravity, and in the shader Godot generated from that material, line three eleven reads it, once per particle, per step, on the GPU. Draw: what each one looks like, here a small gradient streak with a dark rim. That is also why a GPU effect's headless price is near zero. A headless run uses a dummy renderer: it runs no process shader and draws nothing, so the CPU pays only for node bookkeeping.

beats.narration_text: The intent was written before anything was built. Strike: on frame zero, a white flash at the hitbox, at full size. Spray: the sparks fly out forward and a little up, white turning yellow. Fall-off: they arc down under gravity, shrink, turn orange and fade; the last is gone by point four five seconds. Yellow alone barely separates from the wheat and the sky, so every spark carries a dark rim in the art's own line colour. Claude drafted this brief; shuai-z chose the effect and reviewed it.

beats.narration_text: This is the process part, Sparks' process material. Align Y turns each streak along its own velocity. Disable Z keeps every bit of speed in the plane. The direction is nineteen degrees above forward, with a thirty degree spread. Speed between two sixty and four twenty pixels a second, and gravity seven hundred, pulling down. No damping: that is Effect B's feature. And lifetime randomness cuts up to forty percent off some lives.

beats.narration_text: The trigger. Every physics tick, the driver reads whether the sword's hitbox is disabled. Live after disabled is the event, and it fires. Each cut instantiates a new burst, so a fast second cut leaves the first one running: that is the retrigger rule, overlap. It places the burst on the hitbox, and mirrors it with Rudy's facing. The driver sits after Rudy in Main, so it sees the edge on the same tick. It reads his state, and never writes it.

beats.narration_text: Effect B, the same way. Each puff fades in at his feet, then hangs: damping slows it to a stop in the air while it grows. Then it dissipates, lightening toward the ground's colour. For the trail as a whole: a puff within two frames of the first running tick, and after he stops, the trail empties from its old end within half a second. The brief also predicted the dust would show at two point nine to one against the wheat. That prediction did not survive the first strip.

beats.narration_text: The first strip, again a fixture. shuai-z watched it six times at real speed and said: I could not see the dust trail at all. Was it there? Claude rendered the same preview with the dust hidden, and compared them pixel by pixel. At frame twenty-five the dust changed only a hundred and thirty-six pixels by twenty levels or more. The brief's contrast assumed opaque dust over the wheat. The puffs were born in the green grass strip, at three-quarters opacity, with soft edges.

beats.act: Effect B — the process settings, as tuned
beats.narration_text: The dust's process settings, as the three rounds left them. A box emission shape, twenty-eight by six pixels, where the sparks use a point. Straight up, with a fifty degree spread. Speed eighty to one sixty, round three's change. No gravity. And damping, a hundred and twenty to a hundred and eighty pixels per second squared: the feature Effect A does not use. It brakes every puff until it hangs in the air.

beats.narration_text: The condition, in the same driver. Every tick it keeps the emitter at his soles, even when he stands, so a respawn's jump lays down no streak. Running means: in play, on the floor, and moving faster than one pixel a second. It emits only while that holds and the emitter is visible, and it changes emitting only on the tick the answer changes. While the game is paused this script does not run at all, so emitting keeps its value.

beats.act: two lines of the generated process shader
beats.narration_text: The process part, as code. shuai-z converted a copy of Sparks' material into shader code in the editor, and read it. Two lines, beside the brief. Line one thirty-nine picks each particle's speed at random between two uniforms: the brief's two sixty and four twenty. Line three eleven starts the force from the gravity uniform, and a later line adds it to the velocity every step: the brief's seven hundred, down. The numbers are not in the shader's text. They arrive as uniforms, from the material.

beats.narration_text: Now what the tests proved. This is the overlap check in Effect A's state test. It runs the real Main, and cuts through the real slash action: one cut, wait until the swing ends, a second cut, then forty-five ticks. Then it checks that two bursts were alive at the second cut, and that the first was the same node, not moved, and still emitting. It never calls the driver.

beats.narration_text: Headless output, through the course's wrapper. The configuration tests compare every setting with the brief: a hundred and eight for the sparks, sixty-one for the dust. The state tests: fourteen and fourteen, through real input. Two cuts nineteen ticks apart, both bursts alive, the first living its full twenty-seven ticks. Emitting matching the condition on all three hundred and eighty recorded ticks. And the old hundred and forty-one checks, and fifteen, unchanged.

beats.narration_text: Can the checks fail? Eight mutations, and each one exits with one. A Godot 3 name in each scene: it loads without a word, and only the configuration test notices, from the loaded values and a text scan. A value drifted from the brief. One reused burst instead of a new one per cut: six failures. The driver one tick late. The dust's visibility test dropped. Its node moved after Rudy.

shot.observation: Recorded headless output of eight mutations, each exiting 1: two scene mutations per effect (a Godot 3 name, a value drifted from the brief) and two driver mutations per effect (a reused burst, a late driver; a dropped visibility test, a moved node).

beats.narration_text: The prices. Headless, per frame: an empty scene costs point zero zero four milliseconds, the game without the effects about point zero five, and each effect adds less than a hundredth, inside the noise between rounds. The budget, a quarter of a millisecond of GPU time per effect, needed the editor's Visual Profiler. On this M three, its GPU column read zero in every row: the brief's predicted failure twelve. A zero is not a pass, so the budget could not be evaluated here. With vsync off on F nine, the frame rate stayed between two hundred and thirty-nine and four hundred and thirty-eight, but frames per second are not GPU time.

shot.observation: The headless cost table from logs/cost_effects_60fps_rerun.log beside a crop of Codex's Visual Profiler capture (GPU column 0.0 ms) and the FPS fallback with vsync off: 438, 239, 357, 311.

Those were eyes: Codex's captures, and shuai-z's own play, which found the size and the feel of both effects fine.

beats.narration_text: Verdict. Checked by machine: both configuration tests and both state tests pass, the old checks still pass, and eight mutations each fail. Checked by eye: shuai-z judged every round at real speed and played the game. Overruled: Claude read the dust's second round as done; shuai-z said it stayed on the ground, and round three followed. Caught: dust the brief said would show, which shuai-z could not see at all; Effect B, built and tuned but not yet wired in, which shuai-z found missing in the game; Effect B's scene mutations, missed and then run; and Claude's shell, left in a strip folder, which broke shuai-z's command. Uncertain: the GPU price, which this Mac would not report, and nobody else has played it.
